[LLM] Python process contacting AWS IMDS 169.254.169.254 (litellm stealer IAM credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Detects a Python process reaching out to the AWS Instance Metadata Service at 169.254.169.254 — the exact technique the litellm harvester uses to steal IMDSv2 tokens and exchange them for live IAM role credentials. Combined with parent=python this is high fidelity because the legitimate litellm library has no reason to call IMDS directly. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit IMDS abuse: 'IMDS token + IAM role credentials via 169.254.169.254'. Python connecting to the AWS metadata endpoint is unusual — the boto3 SDK normally only does this when explicitly configured (`AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=false`), and litellm proper has no reason to reach for IAM creds. AWS docs confirm the link-local IP semantics; corroborated by Datadog Security Labs and Snyk. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/litellm-credential-stealer-hidden-in-pypi-wheel • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/ • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1528
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^python\d*(\.exe)?$"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, LocalIP
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(WindowsEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 3 and Provider has "Sysmon"
  | extend Image = tostring(EventData.Image), DestIP = tostring(EventData.DestinationIp), User = tostring(EventData.User), CmdLine = tostring(EventData.CommandLine)
  | where DestIP == "169.254.169.254"
  | where Image matches regex @"(?i)\\python\d*\.exe$" or Image matches regex @"(?i)/python\d*$"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Image, CmdLine, DestIP, User),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254"
  | where SrcUsername has "python" or DvcHostname has ""
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, NetworkProtocol, DstPortNumber)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] In-cluster Kubernetes secret enumeration with Python user-agent (litellm stealer K8s pivot) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the litellm stealer's Kubernetes pivot — after reading /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token from inside a compromised pod, it uses the token to call the K8s API and enumerate Secrets across every namespace. Catches both the on-host token read (endpoint platforms) and the resulting mass secret listing from a python-requests user-agent (K8s audit platforms). Rationale: Anchored on two article-specific signals: (1) the exact filesystem path '/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token' the harvester reads, and (2) the article's statement that the stealer makes 'live API calls to enumerate secrets across all namespaces' — which from a python-requests/urllib3 client leaves a recognisable user-agent in K8s audit. Two complementary telemetry vantage points (endpoint file read + control-plane API call) cover both detection layers. Corroborated by Datadog Security Labs and StepSecurity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/litellm-credential-stealer-hidden-in-pypi-wheel • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/24518
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1528 T1613
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath startswith "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount"
   or FileName == "token" and FolderPath has "kubernetes.io/serviceaccount"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^python\d*$"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
let MassThreshold = 3;
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where Verb in~ ("list","get","watch")
| where tostring(ObjectRef.resource) =~ "secrets"
| extend Subject = tostring(User.username)
| where Subject startswith "system:serviceaccount:"
| where UserAgent has_any ("python-requests","Python/","python-urllib3","urllib3","kubernetes/client-python")
| summarize NamespacesQueried = dcount(tostring(ObjectRef.namespace)),
            SecretsCount = count(),
            Namespaces = make_set(tostring(ObjectRef.namespace), 25),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by Subject, UserAgent, _ResourceId
| where NamespacesQueried >= MassThreshold or SecretsCount >= 20
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Python Reads Kubernetes Service Account Token — litellm Stealer K8s Pivot
id: 9f3a2d18-1b8c-4be0-a05e-6cd92c5ec701
description: Detects a python process opening /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. The litellm credential stealer uses this token to call the in-cluster K8s API and enumerate secrets across all namespaces, enabling lateral compromise of every node in the cluster.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/litellm-credential-stealer-hidden-in-pypi-wheel
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/03/24
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1528
logsource:
  category: file_access
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|re|i: '(\\|/)python\d*$'
    TargetFilename: '/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token'
  condition: selection
level: high
(source:kubernetes.audit @verb:(list OR get OR watch) @objectRef.resource:secrets @user.username:system\:serviceaccount\:* @userAgent:(*python* OR *urllib3* OR *kubernetes/client-python*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @file.path:/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token @process.name:(python OR python3))
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo
| TargetFileName=/^\/var\/run\/secrets\/kubernetes\.io\/serviceaccount\/token$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/python\d*$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, UserName, TargetFileName], function=count(as=TokenReads), function=min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen))
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as procs from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token" Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.action
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as procs from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token" Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.action
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Service install for persistence — sc.exe / new service registry write Installation High
Service install with binPath pointing to user-writeable path or LOLBin. Detects via process telemetry (sc.exe create) and registry (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\* writes).
ATT&CKT1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "sc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "create"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
// EventID 4697 is "Service installed" — direct signal, no cmdline-regex needed.
union
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4697
        | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName,
                  Detail = strcat("ServiceName=", ServiceName, " | Image=", ServiceFileName) ),
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where Account !endswith "$"
        | where NewProcessName endswith "\sc.exe" and CommandLine has "create"
        | where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account,
                  Detail = strcat("4688 sc.exe create: ", CommandLine) )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents

| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")

SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688

All release tags in the Checkmarx/kics-github-action repository have been compromised with an infostealer payload. If you are using this Action pinned to any version tag, treat your CI/CD secrets as compromised and rotate immediately.

[LLM] TeamPCP supply-chain C2 — outbound to checkmarx[.]zone / 83.142.209.11 Command & Control High
Hunts CI/CD runner hosts (and any endpoint) connecting to the TeamPCP exfiltration domain checkmarx[.]zone or its hosting IP 83.142.209[.]11, used to receive AES-256-CBC encrypted tpcp.tar.gz archives from compromised Checkmarx/kics-github-action setup.sh runs between 12:58–16:50 UTC on 2026-03-23. Same infrastructure family as the Trivy compromise — actor reuses domain. Rationale: checkmarx[.]zone and 83.142.209.11 are attacker-controlled typosquat exfil infrastructure confirmed by Wiz, Unit 42 and StepSecurity. checkmarx.zone has no legitimate use — any connection to it is high-confidence compromise. Article + Wiz blog cited for IP and domain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/teampcp-attack-kics-github-action • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/teampcp-supply-chain-attacks/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/teampcp-hacks-checkmarx-github-actions.html • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/03/24/detecting-investigating-defending-against-trivy-supply-chain-compromise/

let _badIP = "83.142.209.11";

  ( DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl has _badDomain or RemoteIP == _badIP
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath ),
  ( DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
    | extend Q = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).QueryName)
    | where Q has _badDomain
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl = Q,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath )
| order by Timestamp desc
let _badDomain = "checkmarx.zone";
let _badIP = "83.142.209.11";

    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

        or DestinationDnsDomain has _badDomain
    | project TimeGenerated, Src=SourceIP, Dst=DestinationIP, DstPort=DestinationPort,
              DstHost=DestinationHostName, Url=RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct ),

    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Name has _badDomain
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType ),
  ( ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname, Url ),

    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where SyslogMessage has _badDomain or SyslogMessage has _badIP

[LLM] TeamPCP systemd backdoor — sysmon.py / sysmon.service persistence on CI runner Installation High
Hunts the file-system fingerprint of the TeamPCP persistence stage: a python implant dropped at ~/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py (or /root/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py in K8s pods) and a user-mode systemd unit at ~/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service that polls https://checkmarx[.]zone/raw every 3000 seconds. Both paths are unique to TeamPCP and recur across the Trivy and KICS compromises. Rationale: The path tuple ~/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py + ~/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service is unique to TeamPCP and is documented by Wiz as the persistence mechanism in both the KICS and Trivy compromises. No legitimate Linux software writes both paths. The article references systemd persistence; Wiz provided the exact filenames. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/teampcp-attack-kics-github-action • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/teampcp-supply-chain-attacks/ • https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/from-scanner-to-stealer-inside-the-trivy-action-supply-chain-compromise/
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where ( FolderPath has "/.config/sysmon" and FileName =~ "sysmon.py" )
    or ( FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user" and FileName =~ "sysmon.service" )
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where ( TargetFilePath has "/.config/sysmon" and TargetFileName =~ "sysmon.py" )
    or ( TargetFilePath has "/.config/systemd/user" and TargetFileName =~ "sysmon.service" )
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType,
          TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileSize,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP Systemd Backdoor — sysmon.py / sysmon.service Persistence
id: 7b3d2e4a-1c8f-4a72-9a83-2e9c5b1f0a3d
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of the TeamPCP supply-chain backdoor files dropped by the poisoned Checkmarx/kics-github-action and aquasecurity/trivy-action setup.sh — a python implant at ~/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py and a user-mode systemd unit ~/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service that polls checkmarx.zone/raw for tasking.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/checkmarx-kics-github-action-compromised-malware-injected-in-all-git-tags
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/teampcp-attack-kics-github-action

[LLM] TeamPCP exfiltration archive — tpcp.tar.gz file creation on host Actions on Objectives High
Hunts creation of the AES-256-CBC encrypted exfiltration archive tpcp.tar.gz produced by the compromised setup.sh after harvesting AWS/Azure/GCP credentials, SSH keys, Kubernetes service-account tokens and Runner.Worker memory contents. Same archive name reused in the prior Trivy supply-chain compromise — the static filename is the actor's tradecraft signature. Rationale: tpcp.tar.gz is the literal exfil filename documented by Wiz for both the Trivy and KICS compromises — actor tradecraft signature, not a generic name. The article references the encrypted exfil to checkmarx.zone; Wiz blog supplied the archive filename and the AES-256-CBC mechanism. Pairing a 30-day lookback catches stragglers from compromised pipelines that ran during the 12:58–16:50 UTC window on 2026-03-23. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/teampcp-attack-kics-github-action • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/teampcp-supply-chain-attacks/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/teampcp-hacks-checkmarx-github-actions.html
ATT&CKT1560.001 T1567.002 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where FileName =~ "tpcp.tar.gz"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessParentCreationTime
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where TargetFileName =~ "tpcp.tar.gz"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType,
          TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

CanisterWorm: How a Self-Propagating npm Worm Is Spreading Backdoors Across the Ecosystem

StepSecurity
2026-03-26 7 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Following Trivy's compromise, StepSecurity's AI Package Analyst flagged suspicious new releases across multiple npm scopes — revealing CanisterWorm, a self-propagating npm worm deployed by the TeamPCP threat actor. The worm is a direct continuation of the second Trivy compromise (v0.69.4): attackers embedded a credential harvester in Trivy's CI/CD toolchain, stole npm tokens from affected pipelines, then used those tokens to publish backdoored patch versions across every namespace they could reach — including the @opengov scope (16+ packages).

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)

references:

Trivy Compromised a Second Time - Malicious v0.69.4 Release, aquasecurity/setup-trivy, aquasecurity/trivy-action GitHub Actions Compromised

StepSecurity
2026-03-26 10 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

On March 19, 2026, trivy — a widely used open source vulnerability scanner maintained by Aqua Security — experienced a second security incident. Three weeks after the hackerbot-claw incident on February 28 that resulted in a repository takeover, a new compromised release (v0.69.4) was published to the trivy repository. The original incident disclosure discussion (#10265) was also deleted during this period, and version tags on the aquasecurity/setup-trivy GitHub Action were removed. Trivy maintainers deleted the v0.69.4 tag and Homebrew downgraded to v0.69.3. The following is a factual account…

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — Trivy Compromised a Second Time - Malicious v0.69.4 Release, aquasecurity/setup-
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Compromised trivy binary (v0.69.4-v0.69.6) execution by SHA1 hash · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Trivy supply-chain C2 beacon to typosquat domain scan.aquasecurtiy.org · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GitHub Actions runner credential stealer: python3 base64-decoded payload reading /proc/<pid>/mem · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Trivy supply-chain C2 beacon to typosquat domain scan.aquasecurtiy.org Command & Control High
Hunts any DNS resolution, web request, or outbound socket targeting the attacker-controlled typosquat domain scan.aquasecurtiy.org (note the misspelled 'aquasecurtiy'). This domain received RSA-encrypted GitHub Actions runner secrets harvested by the compromised aquasecurity/trivy-action, aquasecurity/setup-trivy, and trivy v0.69.4-0.69.6 binaries during the March 2026 supply-chain incident. Rationale: The typosquat domain 'aquasecurtiy.org' (misspelled — extra 't' before 'iy') is the single exfiltration channel for every variant of this compromise (trivy-action entrypoint.sh, setup-trivy action.yaml commit 8afa9b9, and trivy v0.69.4-0.69.6 hardcoded). The misspelling is unique enough that any hit anywhere in the estate is a confirmed compromise — independently verified by Aqua Security GHSA, The Hacker News, Snyk and Palo Alto Networks write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/security/advisories/GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/trivy-security-scanner-github-actions.html • https://www.aquasec.com/blog/trivy-supply-chain-attack-what-you-need-to-know/ • https://snyk.io/articles/trivy-github-actions-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/cloud-security/trivy-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1567 T1583.001

  | where RemoteUrl has bad_domain or AdditionalFields has bad_domain
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, ActionType, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName ),
( DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | extend QueryName = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).QueryName)
  | where QueryName has bad_domain
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, ActionType, QueryName,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName )
| order by Timestamp desc
let bad_domain = "aquasecurtiy.org";
union isfuzzy=true
( DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has bad_domain
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCodeName ),
( CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has bad_domain or RequestURL has bad_domain or DestinationDnsDomain has bad_domain
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceAction ),
( ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has bad_domain
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsQueryTypeName ),

  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Url has bad_domain or HttpHostName has bad_domain

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Compromised trivy binary (v0.69.4-v0.69.6) execution by SHA1 hash Installation High
Hunts execution of the malicious trivy binaries released during the March 2026 ecosystem compromise. SHA1 hashes were recovered from the deleted incident discussion #10265 and Docker Hub images aquasec/trivy:0.69.5 and 0.69.6. Any execution of these hashes confirms a compromised CI runner or developer workstation that downloaded trivy during the ~3-hour window. Rationale: Eight SHA1 hashes pre-extracted from the article correspond to the malicious trivy binaries (v0.69.4 GitHub Release + Docker images aquasec/trivy:0.69.5 / 0.69.6) plus modified entrypoint.sh / action.yaml artifacts. Aqua Security advisory GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23 and the Snyk write-up confirm these are the campaign's primary delivery artefacts. Hash match has near-zero FP — only legitimate clean builds re-publishing the same fingerprint could ever collide. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/security/advisories/GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23 • https://www.aquasec.com/blog/trivy-supply-chain-attack-what-you-need-to-know/ • https://snyk.io/articles/trivy-github-actions-supply-chain-compromise/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059

[LLM] GitHub Actions runner credential stealer: python3 base64-decoded payload reading /proc/<pid>/mem Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the credential-stealer execution pattern injected into entrypoint.sh (trivy-action) and action.yaml (setup-trivy@8afa9b9) — bash decodes a base64 Python blob which then opens /proc/<Runner.Worker pid>/mem to extract GitHub Actions secrets marked isSecret:true. Targets Linux self-hosted runners and developer workstations where the action ran outside hosted runner ephemera. Rationale: The article explicitly documents the credential-stealer chain: entrypoint.sh / action.yaml bash decodes a base64 Python blob; the python3 child opens /proc/<Runner.Worker pid>/mem to dump GitHub Actions secrets (StepSecurity Harden-Runner labelled this exact pattern 'Runner Worker Memory Read', PID 2538 → /proc/2167/mem in their controlled replay). The combination of python3-child-of-bash + base64 decode + /proc/<pid>/mem access from a runner working directory is article-specific and not covered by generic LOLBin or LSASS-access rules. Skipped Sigma because the detection requires multi-condition correlation (parent cmdline + child cmdline + path context) rather than a single-event selection block. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/security/advisories/GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23 • https://www.upwind.io/feed/trivy-supply-chain-incident-github-actions-compromise-breakdown • https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/cloud-security/trivy-supply-chain-attack/ • https://mrcloudbook.com/how-trivy-was-compromised-to-deliver-malware-again/
ATT&CKT1003 T1552.001 T1027.013 T1140
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("python3","python")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","Runner.Worker","node","entrypoint.sh")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64","b64decode","/proc/","Runner.Worker","isSecret")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d","base64 --decode","entrypoint.sh","aquasecurity","trivy")
| extend mem_read = iff(ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/\d+/mem", "yes", "")
| extend b64_pipe = iff(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "base64" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "python", "yes", "")
| extend ci_context = iff(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("entrypoint.sh","aquasecurity","trivy","GITHUB_ACTIONS","RUNNER_") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/runner/","/_work/","/_actions/","/home/runner/"), "yes", "")
| where mem_read == "yes" or b64_pipe == "yes" or ci_context == "yes"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          mem_read, b64_pipe, ci_context
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName endswith "python3" or TargetProcessName endswith "python"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "bash" or ParentProcessName endswith "sh" or ParentProcessName endswith "dash" or ParentProcessName has "Runner.Worker" or ParentProcessName endswith "node"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64","b64decode","/proc/","Runner.Worker","isSecret")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d","base64 --decode","entrypoint.sh","aquasecurity","trivy")
| extend mem_read = iff(TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/\d+/mem", "yes", "")
| extend b64_pipe = iff(ParentProcessCommandLine has "base64" and ParentProcessCommandLine has "python", "yes", "")
| extend ci_context = iff(ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("entrypoint.sh","aquasecurity","trivy","GITHUB_ACTIONS","RUNNER_") or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("/runner/","/_work/","/_actions/"), "yes", "")
| where mem_read == "yes" or b64_pipe == "yes" or ci_context == "yes"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, mem_read, b64_pipe, ci_context
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog OR source:windows.sysmon) (@process.name:(python3 OR python) OR @Image:(*python3 OR *python)) AND (@process.parent.name:(bash OR sh OR dash OR Runner.Worker OR node) OR @ParentImage:(*bash OR *sh OR *dash OR *Runner.Worker* OR *node)) AND (@process.command_line:(*base64.b64decode* OR *"base64 -d"* OR *"/proc/"*"/mem"* OR *Runner.Worker* OR *isSecret*) OR @CommandLine:(*base64.b64decode* OR *"base64 -d"* OR *"/proc/"*"/mem"* OR *Runner.Worker* OR *isSecret*))
ENDPOINT

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` 
| where match(parent_cmds, "(?i)trivy|aquasecurity|setup-trivy|entrypoint\\.sh|base64") OR match(cmdlines, "(?i)/proc/[0-9]+/mem|Runner\\.Worker|isSecret|b64decode") 
| sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmds from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("python3","python") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("bash","sh","dash","entrypoint.sh","Runner.Worker","node") AND (Processes.process="*base64.b64decode*" OR Processes.process="*base64 -d*" OR Processes.process="*/proc/*/mem*" OR Processes.process="*Runner.Worker*" OR Processes.process="*isSecret*" OR Processes.parent_process="*base64 -d*" OR Processes.parent_process="*entrypoint.sh*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` 
| where match(parent_cmds, "(?i)trivy|aquasecurity|setup-trivy|entrypoint\\.sh|base64") OR match(cmdlines, "(?i)/proc/[0-9]+/mem|Runner\\.Worker|isSecret|b64decode")

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase

    - attack.t1569.002

    - attack.execution

    category: process_creation

            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'

bittensor-wallet 4.0.2 Compromised on PyPI - Backdoor Exfiltrates Private Keys

StepSecurity
2026-03-26 10 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On March 17, 2026, bittensor-wallet 4.0.2 was identified as a compromised PyPI package. The malicious release had been live on PyPI for approximately 48 hours before being yanked. This post is a ground-up technical breakdown based on a direct diff of the source tarballs for versions 4.0.1 and 4.0.2 — covering exactly what changed, how the backdoor works, and what defenders should do. We also ran the compromised package with StepSecurity Harden Runner and captured every C2 channel firing in real time.

[LLM] bittensor-wallet 4.0.2 backdoor C2 domain contact (opentensor-* lookalikes) Command & Control High
Hunts DNS lookups and outbound connections to the four hard-coded / parent-zone C2 domains used by the bittensor-wallet 4.0.2 PyPI backdoor (opentensor-metrics.com, subtensor-telemetry.com, metagraph-stats.com, opentensor-cdn.com). These domains impersonate legitimate Bittensor infrastructure (opentensor.ai, subtensor, metagraph) and are contacted from python3.12 within ~2 seconds of any coldkey/hotkey decryption. Rationale: All four domains are explicitly named in the article as attacker-controlled lookalike infrastructure confirmed contacted by python3.12 during Harden Runner instrumentation; opentensor-cdn.com is the parent zone for both the DGA rotation (*.opentensor-cdn.com) and the DNS-tunnel egress (t.opentensor-cdn.com), so the suffix match covers all three C2 layers in one rule. No legitimate Bittensor service resolves under these squat zones. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/bittensor-wallet-4-0-2-compromised-on-pypi---backdoor-exfiltrates-private-keys

  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EvtSource="NetConn", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, Indicator=RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | extend QueryName = tolower(tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).QueryName))
  | where isnotempty(QueryName) and QueryName has_any (_c2_domains)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EvtSource="DNS", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, Indicator=QueryName, RemoteIP="", RemotePort=int(0))
| order by Timestamp desc
let _c2_domains = dynamic(["opentensor-metrics.com","subtensor-telemetry.com","metagraph-stats.com","opentensor-cdn.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where isnotempty(DnsQuery) and DnsQuery has_any (_c2_domains)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, EvtSource="ImDns", Indicator=DnsQuery),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, EvtSource="ImNet", Indicator),

[LLM] DNS tunneling exfiltration pattern to *.t.opentensor-cdn.com (hex chunk/index/total/session) Command & Control High
Detects the chunked DNS-A exfiltration channel used by the bittensor-wallet 4.0.2 backdoor when its HTTPS C2 attempts fail. Each NaCl-sealed private-key payload is hex-encoded, split into 60-char chunks, and emitted as A queries shaped <hex>.<index>.<total>.<session_id>.t.opentensor-cdn.com. The regex shape is highly specific and a single match constitutes confirmed exfiltration. Rationale: The article shows 28 real chunks captured by Harden Runner with the exact <hex>.<idx>.<total>.<session>.t.opentensor-cdn.com label shape (session 52016, total 28). The regex matches that schema and only that schema, so a single query is enough to alert; the >=3 chunk threshold in SPL/KQL is purely a noise-floor sanity guard. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/bittensor-wallet-4-0-2-compromised-on-pypi---backdoor-exfiltrates-private-keys
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
| extend QueryName = tolower(tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).QueryName))
| where QueryName endswith ".t.opentensor-cdn.com"
| where QueryName matches regex @"^[0-9a-f]{40,}\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.t\.opentensor-cdn\.com$"
| extend SessionId = extract(@"\.([0-9]+)\.t\.opentensor-cdn\.com$", 1, QueryName)
| extend ChunkTotal = extract(@"\.([0-9]+)\.[0-9]+\.t\.opentensor-cdn\.com$", 1, QueryName)
| summarize ChunkCount = count(),
            Sessions = make_set(SessionId, 10),
            ExpectedTotal = make_set(ChunkTotal, 5),
            SampleQueries = make_set(QueryName, 5),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen  = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where ChunkCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DnsQuery endswith ".t.opentensor-cdn.com"
  | where DnsQuery matches regex @"^[0-9a-f]{40,}\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.t\.opentensor-cdn\.com$"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery),
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Name endswith ".t.opentensor-cdn.com"
  | where Name matches regex @"^[0-9a-f]{40,}\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.t\.opentensor-cdn\.com$"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, SrcIpAddr=ClientIP, DnsQuery=Name)
| extend SessionId = extract(@"\.([0-9]+)\.t\.opentensor-cdn\.com$", 1, DnsQuery)
| extend ChunkTotal = extract(@"\.([0-9]+)\.[0-9]+\.t\.opentensor-cdn\.com$", 1, DnsQuery)
| summarize ChunkCount = count(),
            Sessions = make_set(SessionId, 10),
            ExpectedTotal = make_set(ChunkTotal, 5),
            SampleQueries = make_set(DnsQuery, 5),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen  = max(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr
| where ChunkCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] Compromised bittensor-wallet 4.0.2 source-tarball SHA256 on disk Delivery High
Identifies any host (developer workstation, CI runner, validator/miner box) that has the malicious bittensor-wallet 4.0.2 source tarball or its derived wheel artifacts on disk. Presence of either hash means the backdoored package was downloaded and almost certainly built/installed; any wallet decryption performed while it was active should be treated as a confirmed coldkey/hotkey compromise. Rationale: Both SHA256 values are the pre-extracted IOCs from the StepSecurity post for the malicious 4.0.2 source tarball (primary) and its derived artifact (secondary). Hash equality on a file or process event is a definitive supply-chain compromise indicator with effectively zero false-positive risk. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/bittensor-wallet-4-0-2-compromised-on-pypi---backdoor-exfiltrates-private-keys
