title: bittensor-wallet 4.0.2 Compromised Source Tarball SHA256 Observed
id: b3f4c8d7-2a1e-4b9c-8d52-3e2f1a0b9c87
description: File-create or load-image event whose SHA256 matches the known-bad bittensor-wallet 4.0.2 source tarball / wheel hashes. Any host hitting this rule installed the backdoored package; assume any Bittensor coldkey/hotkey decrypted on that host is leaked.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/bittensor-wallet-4-0-2-compromised-on-pypi---backdoor-exfiltrates-private-keys
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/13
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059.006
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    Hashes|contains:
      - '6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e'
      - 'edc2588d5e272835285e4171dd3daf862149f617015bf52e43d433d8e5c297c5'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - None. Hash matches the malicious artifact only.
level: critical
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) (@Hashes:(*6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e* OR *edc2588d5e272835285e4171dd3daf862149f617015bf52e43d433d8e5c297c5*) OR @file.hash:(6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e OR edc2588d5e272835285e4171dd3daf862149f617015bf52e43d433d8e5c297c5) OR @process.executable.hash.sha256:(6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e OR edc2588d5e272835285e4171dd3daf862149f617015bf52e43d433d8e5c297c5))
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_hash="6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e" OR Filesystem.file_hash="edc2588d5e272835285e4171dd3daf862149f617015bf52e43d433d8e5c297c5") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.user host | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | append [ | tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_hash="6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e" OR Processes.process_hash="edc2588d5e272835285e4171dd3daf862149f617015bf52e43d433d8e5c297c5") by Processes.dest Processes.process Processes.process_hash Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` ]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_hash="6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e" OR Filesystem.file_hash="edc2588d5e272835285e4171dd3daf862149f617015bf52e43d433d8e5c297c5") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.user host | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | append [ | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_hash="6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e" OR Processes.process_hash="edc2588d5e272835285e4171dd3daf862149f617015bf52e43d433d8e5c297c5") by Processes.dest Processes.process Processes.process_hash Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` ]
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("finney.opentensor-metrics.com", "finney.subtensor-telemetry.com", "finney.metagraph-stats.com", "opentensor-cdn.com", "tuwyqibtvy.opentensor-cdn.com", "yccansiwfr.opentensor-cdn.com", "tbqcbkpbhy.opentensor-cdn.com", "t.opentensor-cdn.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["finney.opentensor-metrics.com", "finney.subtensor-telemetry.com", "finney.metagraph-stats.com", "opentensor-cdn.com", "tuwyqibtvy.opentensor-cdn.com", "yccansiwfr.opentensor-cdn.com", "tbqcbkpbhy.opentensor-cdn.com", "t.opentensor-cdn.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("finney.opentensor-metrics.com", "finney.subtensor-telemetry.com", "finney.metagraph-stats.com", "opentensor-cdn.com", "tuwyqibtvy.opentensor-cdn.com", "yccansiwfr.opentensor-cdn.com", "tbqcbkpbhy.opentensor-cdn.com", "t.opentensor-cdn.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("finney.opentensor-metrics.com", "finney.subtensor-telemetry.com", "finney.metagraph-stats.com", "opentensor-cdn.com", "tuwyqibtvy.opentensor-cdn.com", "yccansiwfr.opentensor-cdn.com", "tbqcbkpbhy.opentensor-cdn.com", "t.opentensor-cdn.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("finney.opentensor-metrics.com", "finney.subtensor-telemetry.com", "finney.metagraph-stats.com", "opentensor-cdn.com", "tuwyqibtvy.opentensor-cdn.com", "yccansiwfr.opentensor-cdn.com", "tbqcbkpbhy.opentensor-cdn.com", "t.opentensor-cdn.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("finney.opentensor-metrics.com", "finney.subtensor-telemetry.com", "finney.metagraph-stats.com", "opentensor-cdn.com", "tuwyqibtvy.opentensor-cdn.com", "yccansiwfr.opentensor-cdn.com", "tbqcbkpbhy.opentensor-cdn.com", "t.opentensor-cdn.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e") or SHA1 in~ ("6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e") or MD5 in~ ("6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e") or SHA1 in~ ("6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e") or MD5 in~ ("6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6a416b72ff24804abc12484a3b41413a8580acedd8a5f8c84224fcf0732c2f8e"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase

Malicious npm Releases Found in Popular React Native Packages - 130K+ Monthly Downloads Compromised

StepSecurity
2026-03-26 8 use cases 3 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

On March 16, 2026, StepSecurity Threat Intel was the first to detect and report malicious releases in two popular React Native npm packages — react-native-international-phone-number and react-native-country-select. StepSecurity's AI Package Analyst flagged the compromised versions, and within minutes, StepSecurity filed security issues directly in both GitHub repositories — alerting the maintainer and the community before any other security vendor.

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Compromised react-native-international-phone-number / react-native-country-select files written to node_modules · [LLM] Attacker-controlled scoped npm relay packages on disk (@usebioerhold8733 / @agnoliaarisian7180)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Malicious npm Releases Found in Popular React Native Packages - 130K+ Monthly Do
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm postinstall hook spawning node init.js or child.js (React Native attack pattern)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] node.exe contacting Solana JSON-RPC endpoints (suspected blockchain dead-drop C2) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Compromised react-native-international-phone-number / react-native-country-select files written to node_modules Delivery Medium
Hunts hosts where the two known-compromised React Native npm packages have been installed into a node_modules tree. Article-specific because it targets the two named packages from the StepSecurity disclosure rather than generic npm telemetry; presence alone warrants a developer-workstation review since @latest currently resolves to compromised versions. Rationale: Anchors on the two named compromised npm packages from the article. File-system writes inside node_modules/<pkg>/ confirm the dep is present on a host regardless of which lockfile pinned it; analyst then opens the package.json to confirm the version is one of the listed bad ones (0.11.8 / 0.12.1-3 / 0.3.91 / 0.4.1-2).

[LLM] Attacker-controlled scoped npm relay packages on disk (@usebioerhold8733 / @agnoliaarisian7180) Delivery High
Detects creation of any file under node_modules/@usebioerhold8733/ or node_modules/@agnoliaarisian7180/. These scoped package names were registered exclusively to host the Wave-2/Wave-3 dependency-chain relay (s-format and string-argv hollow clones) and have no legitimate downstream use, making file presence essentially deterministic for compromise. Rationale: These scoped npm names (@usebioerhold8733 and @agnoliaarisian7180) were registered exclusively for the campaign per the StepSecurity disclosure (with matching Proton Mail addresses AgnoliaArisian7180@proton.me). They have zero legitimate downstream consumers, so any on-disk hit is essentially a true positive without requiring version pivot.

[LLM] npm postinstall hook spawning node init.js or child.js (React Native attack pattern) Installation Medium
Catches the moment of payload execution: npm/yarn/pnpm spawning node.exe with init.js or child.js on the command line during a package install. The article documents this exact two-step hook chain (postinstall: node child.js -> exec node init.js) inside the @usebioerhold8733/s-format payload host. Rationale: Anchors on the literal script filenames init.js and child.js called out in the article's payload dependency chain (@usebioerhold8733/s-format -> postinstall: node child.js -> exec node init.js). Constraining the parent to npm/yarn/pnpm lifecycle binaries keeps the FP rate in check while keeping coverage of the postinstall hook itself.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "node.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b(init|child)\.js\b"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","cmd.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm ","yarn ","pnpm ","postinstall")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent

| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"

[LLM] node.exe contacting Solana JSON-RPC endpoints (suspected blockchain dead-drop C2) Command & Control Medium
Hunts node.exe / node processes that talk to public Solana RPC endpoints - the C2 mechanism described in the article ("Solana blockchain C2 malware"). Anchors on the fact that legitimate React Native phone-input / country-select libraries have zero need to contact Solana mainnet. Rationale: Article states the payload is "Solana blockchain C2 malware". Public Solana JSON-RPC endpoints (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com plus the common RPC providers Helius / QuickNode / Alchemy / RPC Pool / Ankr) are the canonical infrastructure any Solana-blockchain dead-drop must contact. A node.exe spawned by an npm postinstall talking to these endpoints on a non-Web3 developer workstation is a sharp anomaly.

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Malicious Polymarket Bot Hides in Hijacked dev-protocol GitHub Org and Steals Wallet Keys

StepSecurity
2026-03-26 8 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The StepSecurity threat intelligence team discovered that dev-protocol — a verified GitHub organization with 568 followers belonging to a legitimate Japanese DeFi project — has been hijacked and is now being used to distribute malicious Polymarket trading bots.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Malicious typosquat npm packages installed on disk (ts-bign / big-nunber / levex-refa / lint-builder)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Malicious Polymarket Bot Hides in Hijacked dev-protocol GitHub Org and Steals Wa
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm postinstall SSH-backdoor chain: node spawning sudo ufw allow 22/tcp + chown ~/.ssh
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 beaconing to Vercel-hosted Cloudflare-impersonating domains (cloudflareguard / cloudflareinsights) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] C2 beaconing to Vercel-hosted Cloudflare-impersonating domains (cloudflareguard / cloudflareinsights) Command & Control High
Detects outbound HTTP(S) traffic or DNS resolution to the two Vercel-hosted C2 domains used by the malicious dev-protocol Polymarket bot supply chain — cloudflareguard.vercel.app (wallet/file exfil) and cloudflareinsights.vercel.app (C2 config + secondary exfil). These hostnames are campaign-exclusive and have no legitimate Cloudflare provenance despite their name. Rationale: Uses the two article-specific C2 hostnames cloudflareguard.vercel.app and cloudflareinsights.vercel.app verbatim — both are campaign-exclusive impersonations of Cloudflare naming. Three external sources (StepSecurity, GetSafety, Medium ADHD/Cyb3rhawk) corroborate the C2 infrastructure. Hostnames alone are sufficient because no legitimate Cloudflare service is hosted under those Vercel subdomains. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-polymarket-bot-hides-in-hijacked-dev-protocol-github-org-and-steals-wallet-keys • https://www.getsafety.com/blog-posts/polymarket-targeted-by-malicious-packages • https://medium.com/adhd-attack-detect-hunt-defend/infrastructure-pivoting-malicious-polymarket-npm-wallet-drainer-and-vidar-stealer-0b222f0e1a53
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1567 T1195.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
let C2Domains = dynamic(["cloudflareguard.vercel.app","cloudflareinsights.vercel.app"]);
let C2UriPaths = dynamic(["/api/scan-patterns","/api/block-patterns","/api/v1"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
  DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains)
     or (RemoteUrl has_any (C2UriPaths) and RemoteUrl has ".vercel.app")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
),
(
  DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | extend Q = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).QueryName)
  | where Q has_any (C2Domains)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Q
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2Domains = dynamic(["cloudflareguard.vercel.app","cloudflareinsights.vercel.app"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
  DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Name has_any (C2Domains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCodeName
),
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (C2Domains)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, EventResult
),
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DstHostname has_any (C2Domains) or Url has_any (C2Domains)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, Url, DstPortNumber
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (C2Domains) or RequestURL has_any (C2Domains)
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] npm postinstall SSH-backdoor chain: node spawning sudo ufw allow 22/tcp + chown ~/.ssh Installation High
Detects the Linux/macOS post-install backdoor sequence emitted by lint-builder's test.js — a node process (typically spawned by npm/sh in a node_modules subdirectory) invoking sudo to enable ufw, open inbound port 22/tcp, and take ownership of the SSH key directory. This sequence is the lint-builder@1.0.1 fingerprint, not generic LOLBin/SSH hardening. Rationale: References the article's exact post-install chain: 'sudo ufw allow 22/tcp', 'sudo ufw enable', 'sudo chown -R runner:runner /home/runner/.ssh', all spawned from node test.js with working directory node_modules/lint-builder. Couples the destructive command with the npm-ancestor pivot so legitimate SSH hardening (rare) doesn't fire. Corroborated by StepSecurity process tree (PIDs 2407→2422→2428→2446→2447→2449→2450) and GetSafety write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-polymarket-bot-hides-in-hijacked-dev-protocol-github-org-and-steals-wallet-keys • https://www.getsafety.com/blog-posts/polymarket-targeted-by-malicious-packages
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546.016 T1098.004 T1562.004 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let SuspectChildCmd = dynamic(["ufw allow 22","ufw allow 22/tcp","ufw enable"]);
let SshChownTokens = dynamic(["/.ssh","/home/runner/.ssh","authorized_keys"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (ProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspectChildCmd))
    or (ProcessCommandLine has "chown" and ProcessCommandLine has_any (SshChownTokens) and ProcessCommandLine has "-R")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","sh","bash","sudo","npm","dash")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node test.js","lint-builder","node_modules")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "node"
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "node_modules"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ChildFile = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          GrandparentFile = InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectChildCmd = dynamic(["ufw allow 22","ufw allow 22/tcp","ufw enable"]);
let SshChownTokens = dynamic(["/.ssh","/home/runner/.ssh","authorized_keys"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcOs has "Linux" or DvcOs has "Mac" or isempty(DvcOs)
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspectChildCmd) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspectChildCmd))
    or ((ActingProcessCommandLine has "chown" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "chown")
        and (ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (SshChownTokens) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (SshChownTokens)))
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("node","sh","bash","sudo","npm","dash")
    or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("node test.js","lint-builder","node_modules")
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node test.js","lint-builder","node_modules")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Malicious typosquat npm packages installed on disk (ts-bign / big-nunber / levex-refa / lint-builder) Delivery High
Hunts for filesystem evidence that any of the four named malicious npm packages from the dev-protocol Polymarket campaign were extracted under a node_modules directory. The four package names are typosquats of big.js and bignumber.js with no legitimate use — any presence in node_modules indicates a victim host that ran npm install against the hijacked repo. Rationale: All four package names (ts-bign, big-nunber, levex-refa, lint-builder) are typosquats explicitly named in the article and corroborated by GetSafety. They have no legitimate publisher on npm, so any node_modules path containing them is high-confidence evidence the host installed the malicious dev-protocol Polymarket repo. Used as a hunt-tier sweep to identify affected developer/CI hosts retroactively. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-polymarket-bot-hides-in-hijacked-dev-protocol-github-org-and-steals-wallet-keys • https://www.getsafety.com/blog-posts/polymarket-targeted-by-malicious-packages
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1608.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let MaliciousPkgs = dynamic(["ts-bign","big-nunber","levex-refa","lint-builder"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
| where FolderPath has_any (MaliciousPkgs)
| extend PkgName = case(
    FolderPath has "node_modules/ts-bign" or FolderPath has @"node_modules\ts-bign", "ts-bign",
    FolderPath has "node_modules/big-nunber" or FolderPath has @"node_modules\big-nunber", "big-nunber",
    FolderPath has "node_modules/levex-refa" or FolderPath has @"node_modules\levex-refa", "levex-refa",
    FolderPath has "node_modules/lint-builder" or FolderPath has @"node_modules\lint-builder", "lint-builder",
    "other")
| where PkgName != "other"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            FileCount = count(), Samples = make_set(FileName, 10),
            CreatingProcess = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 5),
            CreatingCmd = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 5)
            by DeviceName, PkgName
| order by FirstSeen desc
let MaliciousPkgs = dynamic(["ts-bign","big-nunber","levex-refa","lint-builder"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (MaliciousPkgs)
| extend PkgName = case(
    TargetFilePath has "node_modules/ts-bign" or TargetFilePath has @"node_modules\ts-bign", "ts-bign",
    TargetFilePath has "node_modules/big-nunber" or TargetFilePath has @"node_modules\big-nunber", "big-nunber",
    TargetFilePath has "node_modules/levex-refa" or TargetFilePath has @"node_modules\levex-refa", "levex-refa",
    TargetFilePath has "node_modules/lint-builder" or TargetFilePath has @"node_modules\lint-builder", "lint-builder",
    "other")
| where PkgName != "other"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            FileCount = count(),
            Samples = make_set(TargetFileName, 10),
            CreatingProcess = make_set(ActingProcessName, 5)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, PkgName
| order by FirstSeen desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08

DeviceProcessEvents

ForceMemo: Hundreds of GitHub Python Repos Compromised via Account Takeover and Force-Push

StepSecurity
2026-03-26 11 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The StepSecurity threat intelligence team was the first to discover and report on an ongoing campaign — which we are tracking as ForceMemo — in which an attacker is compromising hundreds of GitHub accounts and injecting identical malware into hundreds of Python repositories. The earliest injections date to March 8, 2026, and the campaign is still active with new repos continuing to be compromised.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — ForceMemo: Hundreds of GitHub Python Repos Compromised via Account Takeover and
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] ForceMemo: Node.js v22.9.0 spawned by Python from user home directory · [LLM] ForceMemo: init.json persistence file or i.js loader dropped by Python in user home root · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ForceMemo: Python process queries Solana mainnet RPC endpoint (blockchain dead-drop C2) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
[LLM] ForceMemo: Node.js v22.9.0 spawned by Python from user home directory Installation High
Hunts the ForceMemo payload-execution stage where the obfuscated Python stub downloads Node.js v22.9.0 from nodejs.org, extracts it under the user's home directory, and then invokes the bundled node binary to run the AES-encrypted JS stage. A node binary inside a 'node-v22.9.0-*' folder under a user home, spawned by a python/pip parent, is highly specific to this campaign. Rationale: The 'node-v22.9.0' string is verbatim from StepSecurity's Harden-Runner capture (`/home/runner/node-v22.9.0-linux-x64/bin/node`) and is hard-coded into the malware. Pairing that path with a python/pip parent eliminates any benign Node.js installation. Cross-checked against The Hacker News, SecurityWeek and SCWorld write-ups which all reproduce the same Node.js v22.9.0 download + home-directory extraction behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/glassworm-attack-uses-stolen-github.html • https://www.securityweek.com/forcememo-python-repositories-compromised-in-glassworm-aftermath/ • https://www.scworld.com/brief/glassworm-campaign-evolves-forcememo-attack-targets-python-repositories-via-stolen-github-tokens • https://www.rescana.com/post/glassworm-forcememo-campaign-supply-chain-attack-targets-github-python-repositories-with-stolen-tok/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006 T1105

[LLM] ForceMemo: Python process queries Solana mainnet RPC endpoint (blockchain dead-drop C2) Command & Control High
Hunts the ForceMemo blockchain C2 lookup. After execution, the malware queries the on-chain memo at Solana wallet BjVeAjPrSKFiingBn4vZvghsGj9KCE8AJVtbc9S8o8SC via one of 9 named Solana RPC providers, fetching its current payload URL. A Python (or pip) process contacting any of these RPC endpoints is high-fidelity for non-crypto orgs. Rationale: All 9 RPC FQDNs are verbatim from the StepSecurity write-up and are hard-coded in the malware as a resilient fallback chain. The Solana C2 wallet (BjVeAjPrSKF...8o8SC) is corroborated on-chain and across The Hacker News / SecurityWeek / SCWorld / Rescana. Pairing the destination with a python/pip parent removes the only realistic FP class (legit Web3 devs). Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/glassworm-attack-uses-stolen-github.html • https://www.securityweek.com/forcememo-python-repositories-compromised-in-glassworm-aftermath/ • https://www.rescana.com/post/glassworm-forcememo-campaign-supply-chain-attack-targets-github-python-repositories-with-stolen-tok/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/forcememo-hijacks-github-accounts/
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1071.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution Network_Traffic

    | where RemoteUrl has_any (SolanaRpc)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="Network", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName ),
  ( DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] ForceMemo: init.json persistence file or i.js loader dropped by Python in user home root Installation Medium
Hunts the ForceMemo persistence and JS-loader artefacts. The Python stub writes a JavaScript decryption loader as 'i.js' and a 'init.json' state file with a 2-day recheck timer directly into the user's home directory root. Both filenames are short and generic, but the combination of (python/pip parent) + (filename) + (path = home-directory root, not nested) is highly specific. Rationale: Filenames 'i.js' and 'init.json' and their direct-in-home-root location are verbatim from the StepSecurity write-up ('Writes a JS file (i.js)... Creates a persistence file (~/init.json) with a 2-day recheck timer'). The (python parent) + (home-root, not nested) regex eliminates almost all benign 'init.json' creations, which typically live in app-config or package subdirs. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/glassworm-attack-uses-stolen-github.html • https://www.securityweek.com/forcememo-python-repositories-compromised-in-glassworm-aftermath/ • https://gbhackers.com/forcememo-hijacks-github/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1027 T1059.007

| where FolderPath !has "site-packages" and FolderPath !has "node_modules" and FolderPath !has ".venv" and FolderPath !has "venv"

| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="created" AND Filesystem.file_name IN ("init.json","i.js") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python.exe","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12","python3.13","pip","pip.exe","pip3") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Users\\*\\init.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Users\\*\\i.js" OR Filesystem.file_path="/home/*/init.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="/home/*/i.js" OR Filesystem.file_path="/Users/*/init.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="/Users/*/i.js" OR Filesystem.file_path="/root/init.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="/root/i.js") by host Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="created" AND Filesystem.file_name IN ("init.json","i.js") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python.exe","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12","python3.13","pip","pip.exe","pip3") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Users\\*\\init.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Users\\*\\i.js" OR Filesystem.file_path="/home/*/init.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="/home/*/i.js" OR Filesystem.file_path="/Users/*/init.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="/Users/*/i.js" OR Filesystem.file_path="/root/init.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="/root/i.js") by host Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("217.69.0.159") or RemoteUrl has_any ("")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["217.69.0.159"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic([""]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the

xygeni-action Compromised: C2 Reverse Shell Backdoor Injected via Tag Poisoning

StepSecurity
2026-03-26 8 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The official Xygeni GitHub Action (xygeni-action) was compromised on March 3, 2026, when an attacker using stolen maintainer credentials injected a full C2 reverse shell backdoor and silently moved the mutable v5 tag to the malicious commit - affecting all repositories referencing @v5 without any visible change to their workflow files. The v5 tag remains poisoned as of March 9; users should immediately pin to v6.4.0 or a specific commit SHA, and StepSecurity's Harden-Runner would have detected and blocked the C2 callback to 91.214.78.178.

ATT&CKT1027 T1190 T1195.002
Domainssecurity-verify.91.214.78.178.nip.io
IPs91.214.78.178

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] GitHub Actions workflow file referencing compromised xygeni/xygeni-action@v5 or backdoored commit 4bf1d4e
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — xygeni-action Compromised: C2 Reverse Shell Backdoor Injected via Tag Poisoning
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound C2 callback to xygeni-action backdoor IP 91.214.78.178 from CI runner · [LLM] Bash-spawned curl to xygeni-action C2 nip.io endpoint with /b/in /b/q /b/r path on CI runner · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Outbound C2 callback to xygeni-action backdoor IP 91.214.78.178 from CI runner Command & Control High
Detects any outbound connection from a host (typically a CI/CD runner) to the xygeni-action C2 infrastructure: the literal IP 91.214.78.178 or any nip.io wildcard subdomain wrapping that IP (e.g. security-verify.91.214.78.178.nip.io). The implant registers via POST /b/in then polls /b/q every 2-7s for 3 minutes. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim C2 IP (91.214.78.178) and the nip.io wildcard FQDN (security-verify.91.214.78.178.nip.io) named in the article. The IP belongs to attacker-controlled infrastructure and nip.io subdomains embedding that IP only exist for the purpose of evading IP-block lists; no legitimate enterprise traffic should resolve them. Cross-checked with StepSecurity's incident write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/xygeni-action-compromised-c2-reverse-shell-backdoor-injected-via-tag-poisoning
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090 T1568.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "91.214.78.178"
   or RemoteUrl has "91.214.78.178.nip.io"
   or RemoteUrl has "security-verify.91.214.78.178"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousIP = "91.214.78.178";
let MaliciousFqdn = "91.214.78.178.nip.io";
union isfuzzy=true
(ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr == MaliciousIP or DstHostname has MaliciousFqdn or Url has MaliciousFqdn
    | extend Host = DvcHostname, Src = SrcHostname, DstIp = DstIpAddr, DstHost = DstHostname, DstPort = tostring(DstPortNumber), MatchUrl = Url
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable = "ImNetworkSession", Host, Src, DstIp, DstHost, DstPort, MatchUrl),
(CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP == MaliciousIP or DestinationHostName has MaliciousFqdn or RequestURL has MaliciousFqdn
    | extend Host = SourceHostName, Src = SourceIP, DstIp = DestinationIP, DstHost = DestinationHostName, DstPort = tostring(DestinationPort), MatchUrl = RequestURL
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable = "CommonSecurityLog", Host, Src, DstIp, DstHost, DstPort, MatchUrl),
(Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where SyslogMessage has MaliciousIP or SyslogMessage has "91.214.78.178.nip.io" or SyslogMessage has "security-verify.91.214.78.178"
    | extend Host = HostName, Src = HostName, DstIp = MaliciousIP, DstHost = "", DstPort = "", MatchUrl = SyslogMessage
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable = "Syslog", Host, Src, DstIp, DstHost, DstPort, MatchUrl)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GitHub Actions workflow file referencing compromised xygeni/xygeni-action@v5 or backdoored commit 4bf1d4e Delivery High
Detects on-disk evidence that a self-hosted runner has checked out (or that a developer workstation has cloned) the xygeni/xygeni-action repo at the poisoned v5 tag or the backdoored commit 4bf1d4e from PR #48, prior to or independent of network detection. Pre-execution catch. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim repo path (xygeni/xygeni-action), the poisoned mutable tag (v5), and the backdoored commit SHA prefix (4bf1d4e) explicitly named in the article. Excludes the post-incident clean release (commit 13c6ed2 / v6.4.0) and the legitimate frozen v5.38.1 release to suppress benign reads of the same repo. Cross-checked with the StepSecurity tag-state inventory. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/xygeni-action-compromised-c2-reverse-shell-backdoor-injected-via-tag-poisoning

   or FolderPath has "4bf1d4e"

[LLM] Bash-spawned curl to xygeni-action C2 nip.io endpoint with /b/in /b/q /b/r path on CI runner Command & Control High
Detects the live xygeni-action implant in execution: a bash subshell on a CI runner calling curl with -sfk -m8 against security-verify.91.214.78.178.nip.io on the /b/in registration, /b/q polling, or /b/r results-post paths described in the obfuscated action.yml payload. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim implant artefacts: the curl invocation pattern (`curl -sfk -m8 -H "$_k"`), the C2 FQDN (security-verify.91.214.78.178.nip.io) and the three application paths (/b/in, /b/q, /b/r) named in the obfuscated action.yml. Parent-process is almost always /bin/bash spawned by the GitHub Actions Runner.Worker because the action.yml step declares `shell: bash`. Cross-checked with StepSecurity's payload annotation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/xygeni-action-compromised-c2-reverse-shell-backdoor-injected-via-tag-poisoning
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "91.214.78.178.nip.io"
   or ProcessCommandLine has "security-verify.91.214.78.178"
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "91.214.78.178" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/b/in","/b/q","/b/r"))
| extend ParentIsShell = InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","ash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ParentIsShell
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("curl","wget")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "91.214.78.178.nip.io"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has "security-verify.91.214.78.178"
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "91.214.78.178" and (ActingProcessCommandLine has "/b/in" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "/b/q" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "/b/r"))
| extend ParentIsShell = ParentProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","ash")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentIsShell
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
